content_sections.body_text: A minimal pair changes one sound. Tim /tɪm/ has a short vowel; team /tiːm/ has a longer vowel. Ship /ʃɪp/ and sheep /ʃiːp/ use the same contrast. Say each pair slowly. Keep the other sounds unchanged.
content_sections.title: Hear one-sound contrasts

content_sections.body_text: A: ‘Team?’ B: ‘Tim—short /ɪ/. I’m Tim.’ A: ‘Tim. Nice to meet you.’ Then: A: ‘Your job?’ B: ‘I work on a ship—short /ɪ/, not sheep /iː/.’ The sound choice matters because it changes the name or meaning.
content_sections.title: Use the contrast to clarify

content_sections.body_text: Write the two words in each pair on separate cards. Record them in mixed order, leaving a pause. Later, play the recording without looking and point to the word you hear; reveal your speaking list to check. Re-record unclear items, making /iː/ longer without changing the final sound.
content_sections.title: Perceive, check, repeat

content_sections.body_text: Create a three-turn introduction using Tim or a short-/ɪ/ word connected to a job or place. Include one clarification turn, then speak both roles without reading. Success: the listener choice matches your intended word twice, the correction is polite and clear, and both speakers take a turn.
content_sections.title: Personal-information outcome
